requirement: An online store manages customers and their orders. Each customer has a Customer ID, Name, Email, and Phone Number. A customer can place many orders, each with an Order Number, Order Date, Status, and Total Amount. Every order belongs to exactly one customer.

A shop records the products that appear on each order. Each product has a Product ID, Name, and Unit Price. Each order has an Order Number and Order Date. An order can contain many products and a product can appear on many orders; for each product on an order the system stores the Quantity and the Price at purchase.

A catalog organizes products into categories. Each category has a Category ID, Name, and Description. Each product has a Product ID, Name, Price, and Description, and belongs to exactly one category. A category can contain many products.

A marketplace manages a shopping cart for each customer. Each customer has a Customer ID and Name. Each product has a Product ID, Name, and Price. A customer has one active cart identified by a Cart ID with a Created Date; the cart can hold many products, and for each product the cart stores the Quantity added.

An online retailer processes payments for orders. Each order has an Order Number, Order Date, and Total Amount. Each payment has a Payment ID, Payment Date, Amount, and Method, and settles exactly one order. An order is paid by a single payment.

A retailer tracks inventory across warehouses. Each warehouse has a Warehouse ID, Name, and Location. Each product has a Product ID and Name. A product can be stocked in many warehouses and a warehouse stocks many products; for each product in a warehouse the system records the Quantity On Hand and Reorder Level.

A store collects product reviews from customers. Each customer has a Customer ID and Name. Each product has a Product ID and Name. A customer can review many products and a product can be reviewed by many customers; each review has a Rating, Comment, and Review Date.

An online store offers discount coupons. Each coupon has a Coupon Code, Discount Percentage, and Expiry Date. Each order has an Order Number and Total Amount. A coupon can be applied to many orders, but each order applies at most one coupon.

A store ships orders to customer addresses. Each customer has a Customer ID and Name. Each address has an Address ID, Street, City, and Postal Code, and belongs to one customer; a customer can have many addresses. Each order with an Order Number and Order Date is shipped to exactly one address.

A marketplace lists products sold by vendors. Each vendor has a Vendor ID, Name, and Contact Email. Each product has a Product ID, Name, and Price, and is sold by exactly one vendor. A vendor can list many products.

A store manages product variants such as size and color. Each product has a Product ID, Name, and Base Price. Each variant has a SKU, Size, Color, and Stock Quantity, and belongs to exactly one product. A product can have many variants.

A retailer tracks shipments for orders. Each order has an Order Number and Order Date. Each carrier has a Carrier ID, Name, and Phone Number. A shipment has a Shipment ID, Ship Date, Tracking Number, and Status; each shipment delivers one order and is handled by one carrier.
